name: Slip casting
summary: Liquid clay is poured into a plaster mould. The plaster takes water from the clay and a wall forms on the inside of the mould.
how: Make a plaster mould in two or more parts.
Pour slip into the mould and wait 10 to 20 minutes for a wall of 3 to 5 mm.
Pour out the rest of the slip.
Open the mould when the clay is leather-hard and fettle the seam.

origin.note: Potters of Staffordshire start to cast earthenware in plaster moulds.

adoptions.via: Staffordshire potters cast and press earthenware figures in plaster moulds, so that one model gives many figures.
Parian makers cast figures from a thin slip in plaster moulds and fire them without a glaze.
Sanitary works cast WC pans, basins and cisterns in plaster moulds, so that one model gives many identical pieces.
Fireclay works cast the sink as one thick piece in a large plaster mould.
The works of T. G. Green casts jugs and teapots of Cornishware in plaster moulds and then bands them by hand.
Factories cast deco dancers and gazelles in plaster moulds, and paint each one by hand.
Works cast the basin, the pan and the bath of a set in plaster moulds and spray each with the same coloured glaze.
